walkthroughs.body_html:
Exploring the Solar System — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Exploring the Solar System brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Exploring the Solar System.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Length of the solar cycle (sunspot count)?
options: 1 year
11 years
22 years
50 years

mcqs.q: Charged particles streaming from the Sun are called?
options: Solar flares
Solar wind
Aurora
Cosmic rays

mcqs.q: Why is Jupiter classified as a gas giant?
options: Its bulk is mostly hydrogen and helium with no defined solid surface.
It is the hottest stage.
It is mostly air like Earth's atmosphere.
It is made of fire.

mcqs.q: What is the principle behind stellar parallax?
options: A nearby star appears to shift against background stars as Earth orbits the Sun.
Telescopes distort star positions.
Stars actually move position throughout the year.
It is made of fire.

mcqs.q: What defines a star as being on the 'main sequence'?
options: It is the largest stage of a star's life.
Telescopes distort star positions.
It fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.
It is the hottest stage.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Solar wind”?
options: ~11-year cycle of sunspot number and magnetic activity; full magnetic cycle is 22 years.
Continuous stream of charged particles flowing from the Sun's corona at 400-800 km/s.
Sudden intense burst of X-ray and UV radiation from magnetic reconnection above sunspots.
Cooler regions (~3,800 K) on the photosphere with strong magnetic fields (~0.3 T).
